gaps: Division presidents not found in any public source for: Raleigh, Charleston, Myrtle Beach, Tampa / Southwest Florida, Greensboro (Starlight only), Tucson (Starlight only), Denver (start-up; only the land VP is named).

Charleston: Robert Norton, the former Ashton Woods Coastal Carolinas division president who grew Charleston from start-up to 700+ annual closings, left to join Tri Pointe in Aug 2025 (https://rss.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/08/19/3135535/0/en/tri-pointe-homes-names-robert-norton-as-division-president-of-coastal-carolinas.html). His successor is not public. The company was hiring a Charleston VP of Finance in Oct 2026.

Raleigh: the last named leaders are stale. Jason Morrow became Starlight Homes Raleigh Division President and Trey McDonald joined Starlight Raleigh leadership through the Capitol City Homes asset acquisition (Dec 2021, https://rss.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/12/02/2345159/32264/en/ashton-woods-usa-l-l-c-acquires-the-assets-of-capitol-city-homes.html). Neither was confirmed in 2025 or 2026, so they are left out.

Regional presidents: only Texas (Motley) and Florida and Tennessee (Fitzpatrick) are published. No regional leader is named for Georgia, the Carolinas or Arizona, so those division presidents are inferred to report to COO Ryan Lewis.

Division land heads (VP Land Acquisition / Land Development / Entitlement): only Denver (Shannon Robbins) is confirmed current. Jacob O'Keefe was named Jacksonville VP of Land Acquisition in Aug 2023 (https://www.ashtonwoods.com/news/ashton-woods-continues-its-florida-expansion-into-jacksonville), but no 2025 or 2026 source confirms him, so he is left out. The Org shows a 26-person 'Land Development & Acquisition' team but does not publish the names. Per the company's annual report, each division has its own land acquisition and development staff, with corporate approving every land deal.

Unplaced division presidents: ZoomInfo (page dated Nov 2026) lists John Reny and Joseph Killinger as Division President with no division. Reny ran Atlanta from 2020 and was Florida division president for 16 years before that. Both are left out of this file because their geography is unknown (they appear in ashton-woods.people.json).

San Antonio: Paul Lock (Division President for both brands) appears in a search snippet with tenure 06/2023 to 09/2025, so he has probably been succeeded by Manny Alarcon. The bold.pro page did not load to confirm this.
Nashville: there is a conflict between David Bracht (company release, June 2024) and Will Coles (directory, undated). Neither is confirmed by the company in 2025 or 2026.

Starlight Homes has no separate brand president. Division presidents run both brands in each market (e.g. Austin), and the Texas regional president covers both brands. Starlight-only markets are Greensboro and Tucson.
Lead not used: Matt Linaman represents Starlight Homes on the 2026 HBA of Central Arizona board (https://www.hbaca.org/board-of-directors/), but his Starlight title is not published.

State registries: Texas Comptroller officer records for every Ashton/Starlight Texas entity list only CEO Ken Balogh and CFO Zack Sawyer (2026), with no division officers. Florida corporate records were not checked.
Division leaders in Raleigh, Charleston, Myrtle Beach, Tampa, Greensboro and Tucson: not confirmed from local press. Most divisions are placed only by The Org location fields (tagged Inferred).
